title: By the pen
hook: by the pen and what they write (68:1)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the birds held by ar-Rahman, and your line: held by the merciful. Did a bird catch your eye? Today a new surah, and it opens with an oath. Day six hundred forty.

When people swear an oath, they swear by something big. By God. By my mother's life. On the Bible, on the Qur'an, on everything I love. Several surahs of the Qur'an open with an oath by grand things: the sun, the dawn, the night, the stars. Then there's surah sixty-eight. It swears by an object you probably have in a drawer, a bag, or behind your ear right now. A pen. And by what people write with it.

Surah al-Qalam, the Pen, verse one, in Pickthall's translation: "Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therewith)." It starts with a single letter, nun, one of the separate letters that open some surahs. What it means, the Qur'an doesn't say. Some scholars say only Allah knows; early commentators offered guesses, an inkwell, a great fish, and the guesses stayed guesses. Then the oath: wa al-qalam, by the pen. Think about where this was heard. Mecca was a place of memory and speech, where poets recited aloud, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself is described in the Qur'an as unlettered. And yet the revelation keeps pointing at writing. The verses tradition counts as the first revealed, in surah al-'Alaq, say that the Most Generous taught by the pen, taught people what they did not know. Here the pen is something to swear by. A hadith in Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi goes further: the first thing Allah created was the pen, and it was told to write. Scholars discuss what that pen is; it isn't pictured as an ordinary one. But the honor reaches the ordinary one too. A scrawled grocery list, a letter to a grandmother, a page of notes before an exam: all of it belongs to what the verse calls that which they write. The oath takes in that whole list.
screen: `BY THE PEN, AND WHAT THEY WRITE.`

segments.voice: The practice: write one grateful line. Find a pen if you can, and something to write on, the back of a receipt is fine. If you only have a phone, that's fine too, but a pen is better today. Sit for a moment and let one thing you're grateful for rise up. Then write it in a single line, slowly, letter by letter, as if the writing mattered. Read it back once. The bell holds the time.
Al-Qalam. The Pen, opening with the letter nun and an oath by the pen and what people write, from a revelation that says Allah taught by the pen. Today's word.

Your line: even your grocery list counts. Today, write one thing by hand that you'd normally type: a note to someone, a list, a line of thanks. Notice it takes longer, and that's fine. Day six hundred forty.

howItsDone: Muslims hold writing in high honor: the verses tradition counts as the first revealed mention the pen, surah 68 swears by it, and calligraphy, above all of the Qur'an, is a treasured art.
